executive_summary: Your supply chain is caught between two distinct pressures: geopolitical fragmentation affecting most of your critical suppliers, and unexplained equity volatility in a few high-exposure vendors that warrants immediate investigation. The geopolitical cluster is substantial—nearly all your printing substrates, nicotine, EMS, and battery suppliers sit in contested regions (China trade-war exposure, Russia-NATO proximity in Finland, India border tensions, South Africa infrastructure collapse)—but these are chronic conditions you likely already manage. What needs urgent attention is the equity sell-offs in Smoore (-2.7%), AMCOR (-1.8%), and Texas Instruments (-1.7%), all in critical or high-exposure categories; unexplained stock movements this sharp often precede supply warnings or financial distress, and you should contact these suppliers directly for color on cash position, production capacity, and forward guidance within 48 hours. De-risk China-sourced EMS and batteries (Huizhou BYD, Smoore, EVE Energy) by stress-testing alternative suppliers or inventory buffers, since US export controls could tighten faster than geopolitical signals suggest. Stora Enso and Sappi present lower urgency—Nordic and South African disruptions move slowly—but flag both for Q2 contingency planning.
